     (a) the EXACT iter574 anti-pattern — full WRONG ❌ code block with `CURRENT_DATE AS day` in daily_active CTE then `LEFT JOIN ... ON c.day = d.day` — explains only today's row matches, every other day is COALESCE(NULL,0)=0; RIGHT ✅ = the range-join query above where c.day appears IN the join predicate.
     (b) BETWEEN closed-interval ban — `BETWEEN s.start AND s.end` double-counts the boundary day (a subscription ending on X AND one starting on X both count on X); RIGHT ✅ = half-open `s.start <= c.day AND (s.end IS NULL OR s.end > c.day)`; also notes BETWEEN does not handle NULL end natively.
  7. CONTRAST card — 3-row table side-by-side: Forward-fill (LAST_VALUE IGNORE NULLS / look-back frame) vs Running total (SUM OVER ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) vs Interval-overlap (range JOIN start<=d AND end>d + GROUP BY + COUNT). 'Use when' clause for each. Closing line: 'If your question reads "what was X as of each day d?" think first: VALUE I'm carrying forward / ACCUMULATION / COUNT of intervals covering d. The three are not interchangeable.'
  8. Optional perf note — boundary-event cumulative form (+1 at start, -1 at end, running SUM over event_date) as a scalable alternative for very large interval tables; framed as alternative, not over-elaborated.
